messages:
sam: ran a mixed-sequence sweep across A100/H100/L40S this morning. goal was to stress kernel selector + kv-cache under batch-stride patterns. immediate thing: L40S flips into paged_fused at seq>4096 and batch>=8 and we see memory thrash + fallback to tiled_naive twice per minute. logs attached inline below.

maria: ugh that's the cold-start/eviction loop we've seen with long-tailed sequences. do you have the exact runpack (seq distribution + batch stride)?

sam: here's the minimal repro we used:

```bash
REDWOOD_RUN=1 ./run_bench --model=redwood/open-7b --gpus=A100,H100,L40S \
  --seq-dist=mixed --seq-buckets=512,1024,2048,4096,8192 \
  --batch-sweep=1,2,4,8,16 --iters=120 --kv-mode=paged
```

sam: quick pasted perf (median tokens/sec) by device for seq=8192: 
A100  batch=8 -> 1250 tok/s (fused_flash)
H100  batch=8 -> 1390 tok/s (fused_flash + fp8 path)
L40S batch=8 -> 420 tok/s (paged_fused -> fallback tiled_naive under thrash)

alex: that L40S number is _way_ lower than expected. did the kernel selector pick a suboptimal kernel because of the batch-stride distribution? maybe a heuristic threshold misclassification.

sam: yes the selector picked paged_fused for L40S initially, but memory allocs peaked and we observed kvcache evictions. when eviction rate spikes, we see two behaviors: 1) heavy memcpy stalls, 2) runtime switches to tiled_naive to avoid OOM. both hurt latency and throughput.

jia: any nvprof/trace? curious if the memcpy is synchronous or using async streams. also want to see if the KV cache metadata is getting fragmented (small allocations).

sam: pasted trimmed trace snippet: 

```
[176] device L40S alloc 1.2G -> ok
[177] device L40S alloc 2.8G -> ok
[178] kvcache evict 512MB (age=0.2s)
[179] memcpy H2D 512MB @ 0.8s (blocking)
[180] kernel paged_fused launch (sm occupancy 60%) -> 30ms
[181] runtime detect high-evict -> switch kernel policy -> tiled_naive
[182] tiled_naive launch -> 120ms
[183] throughput drop observed 75% for next 3 iters
```

maria: hmm looks like memcpy is blocking the queue. we recently changed the batching heuristic to prefer larger global batch strides to boost amortized kernel overhead — that might be forcing bigger intermediate buffers on L40S. can we rerun with batch-stride cap for L40S?

sam: tried cap 4 on L40S (same run but --device-config L40S:max_batch_stride=4). result: evictions down 90%, throughput up to 980 tok/s for batch=4 at seq=8192, but latency jitter still present on cold-start.

alex: good signal. hypothesis: selector threshold for paged_fused on L40S needs to incorporate recent eviction rate, not just static seq+batch heuristics. we should add a moving window metric into the policy.

perf-bot: regression detector: "attn-prefetch-heuristic" commit 0a3f9b introduced larger prefetch buffers on mixed workloads (detected 2026-03-07). Alert score: medium.

jia: can someone bisect that commit locally? if it added aggressive prefetch for mixed sequences, it explains the giant buffer sizes. if we revert prefetch increase for devices with small VRAM (L40S) we might avoid thrash.

sam: assigned to @jia to do a quick bisect and a microbench. I'll open a short perf-run job and tag results.

jia: will run bisect + nvprof tonight and post summary. immediate next action: add a quick guard in selector: if recent_evictions > 2 in last 30s -> prefer lower-prefetch kernel or cap stride. that should be a fast mitigation for Canary.

maria: +1. Also let's add a perf test: mixed-seq long-tail on L40S with batch sweep and eviction counters as assertion. If eviction > threshold mark run as flaky/regressed.

sam: makes sense. I'll add the test to the nightly perf suite and include the CLI repro. will post run id when done. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: scheduled nightly job 2329004-eviction-guard-test (L40S) queued

alex: thanks team. if bisect shows the prefetch change, let's prepare a targeted rollback patch and a config knob per device class. no need to risk H100/A100 performance.

sam: agreed. wrapping up for now — will update once tests run.
